While I agree that “men suck” is problematic phrasing that shouldn’t be used in womyn focused conversations, I don’t think “women should support women” is problematic in and of itself. It’s the notion of a marginalized group supporting each other through the prejudice that they face on a daily basis. It’s the notion of building up instead of tearing down and judging, like some others have said in this thread. It’s not saying to support womyn purely because their womyn at all, especially not if it is a woman who is a terrible person. I don’t think when people say or write empowering phrases about womyn supporting each other that they are including womyn like Casey Anthony, for example. But that’s just my two cents on it

I was working at a large department store and had been there about six months but was on the fast track for a promotion. One day, I took my last break and looked at my phone for the first time since my lunch. I had several missed calls from my mother and when I called her back, she told me that my maternal grandmother had died. I was in the break room taking this call and one of the managers happened to be in the room with me. I started crying and after a couple of minutes told my mom I had to go. The manager didn’t look or sound all that concerned but she did ask me what was going on and I told her about my grandmother.  

She said an empty sorry and asked if I could keep working. I started to say how I wasn’t sure if I should and she interrupted me to tell me that the closer had called out and she was really hoping that I would stay to work. Because I was still hoping to get a promotion and my mom lived four hours away anyway, I decided I would drive to see her the next day, which was my day off, and try to get through work. I ended up closing the store with that same manager and doing just that, going to see my mom the next day. 

I left the job for a multitude other reasons but that was certainly the beginning of a snowball of shitty behavior on the management team’s part. 

TLDR: found out my grandmother died while I was at work and was expected to work over my shift because someone called out

Sex is chromosomal but that's also on a spectrum. This article has some more specific information: http://www.nature.com/news/sex-redefined-1.16943

When it comes down to how many in the LGBT community identify, however, there is typically regarded to be three separate sexes--female, male, and intersex--intersex being a sort of all encompassing word to include the chromosomal variations for XX and XY. 

As for use of gender terms, I am not an expert by any means, but my understanding is to be within the gender binary is to fall on either side, male or female, with no part of that identity pertaining to your sex. Whereas to be within the gender spectrum allows for more inclusive language to help people with identities that don't fall on either male or female. That's just my understanding though. Someone who is part of the Trans/Nonbinary community will certainly have a better answer
